note.p: Ed Pope notes: 10.12.1795 Godwin calls on / then no Bacon till 1822 see letter from Samuel Parr to Godwin (Abinger c.2 f.136-7) dated 16.12.1795. John Bacon ODNB 1740-1799 was working on the sculpture of Dr Samuel Johnson in St Paul's cathedral for which Dr Samuel Parr had written the inscription. Parr asked Godwin to check on it for him.

Bacon dies in 1799, but his son - also John Bacon (1777-1859) was also a sculptor and undertook work in Both Westminster Abbey and St Pauls (see ODNB). He has two chance meetings with him in October 1823 and then has tea with him, at which John Bacon's son, John Bacon, is also present. The ODNB suggests that Bacon became reclusive and focused on ecclesiastical and architectural masonry and sculpture. We believe, nonetheless, that this is the same Bacon whom Godwin sees a little in 1823 (mainly advs and at other venues, but not exclusively), and diminishingly thereafter.
